newsitem.title: ITALY: Safilo sees H1 sales continuing to rise.
newsitem.headline: Safilo sees H1 sales continuing to rise.

text.p: Italian spectacle frame maker Safilo continues to see a good trading performance despite the weakness during the last few months in the spectacle sector.
Safilo said in May group sales rose some 32 percent in the first four months of 1996, and it said on Monday figures for the first six months of 1996 will see a similar trend.
"The rise in the first half is in line with the rise in the first four months," said Safilo chairman Vittorio Tabacchi in an interview with Reuters.

In 1996 group sales are seen quite a bit above the forecast 550 billion lire forecast. A year earlier sales were at 416.4 billion lire. The company's aim is to raise turnover to one trillion lire in 1998.
"The group is showing strong growth and we confirm the decision not to go to the market to finance recent acquisitions," Tabacchi added.

The acquisition of U.S. sports sunglasses group Smith Sport and the Austrian group Carrera Optyl prompted some market players to think the group might come to the market for capital, but the group said it would not seek funds from shareholders.
The acquisitions cost Safilo 100 billion lire, but in 1995 the group's cash flow reached 60 billion lire.
Safilo was one of best performing stocks on the Milan bourse last year.
